system_context.fact: Production entry creates telegram.New(cfg.Telegram, telegram.NoBusinessUpdates), facade.New(telegramRepo), tgrpc.New(facadeService) and pb.RegisterFacadeGRPCServer. The new streaming handlers are reachable through the existing singleton Repo/session and no new business-update consumer is introduced.

App owns app-local DTOs, message media resolution, the two public streaming methods and the private progressive core. The core starts DownloadFile asynchronously with Priority 16/Offset 0/Limit 0/Synchronous false, emits startup metadata, samples GetFile before every prefix query, caps reads at 256 KiB, emits synchronously, advances the cursor only after a successful emit, handles complete/unknown-size/empty/inactive/overflow cases and uses a context-aware 250 ms timer.

Transport owns request validation, one app-event-to-one-pb-event mapping, sequential Send, first-Send-error precedence, stable download-failure messages, flood-wait preservation, Canceled/DeadlineExceeded mapping and the generated server-stream handlers. The generated interface assertion is at line 37.

Infra exposes exactly the four raw file primitives with pinned SDK signatures. DownloadFile already existed; GetFile, GetFileDownloadedPrefixSize and ReadFilePart are added with FloodWaitFromError and no withChatReady, matching the chat-less file-operation policy. No GetFileMimeType or CancelDownloadFile is present.

Both replacement RPCs are server streams returning FileDownloadEvent. The oneof has metadata/chunk/complete with the locked field numbers. All 15 fbc22cc RPC lines remain and the fbc22cc proto diff is additions-only (36 lines, no deletions).
Generated client and server interfaces use grpc.ServerStreamingClient/ServerStreamingServer for FileDownloadEvent, matching the app/transport signatures.

A1 uses real facade.Service + real Transport + generated client over bufconn, one synctest bubble per ordinary subtest, a 5 s virtual context deadline, an async fake that blocks only when Synchronous=true, a one-byte pre-completion prefix, a nonempty-payload-before-release assertion with PROGRESSIVE_PAYLOAD_BEFORE_COMPLETION, an async-request assertion, exact final bytes, and release/conn/server/listener cleanup.

App tests cover progressive prefix exposure and bounded reads, unknown-size remaining bytes, complete empty files, terminal failures, read errors, cancellation/deadline cases, callback backpressure, completion races and two concurrent readers of the same fake file.

The script runs only TestProgressiveDownloadBeforeCompletion, requires exactly one Synchronous:false mutation, uses an EXIT restore trap, requires a nonzero red run with the named test failure and marker, rejects build/setup/panic/timeout/no-test red reasons and unrelated failures, verifies byte restoration, and requires a final green run.

The only workflow change is one 'Progressive download red-green proof' step invoking bash scripts/verify-facade-streaming.sh after the existing go test ./internal/... step. The CMake policy override, pins, cache keys, parallel build, install/archive, triggers, permissions, go vet and go test remain present.

The acceptance client is cgo-free (pb/grpc/std only), uses signal and timeout context, creates .part exclusively, writes bounded sequential chunks, hashes incrementally, rejects metadata/chunk/complete/EOF violations and non-OK status, preserves the partial file on error, and renames only after clean EOF plus optional digest verification.
